The mock is a six-beat landing rhythm — nav / hero (fixed 640 copy + a 544 proof card that is a small illustrated case study ending in "I have a similar project →") / ink stats band / 6 illustrated industry cards / ink closing band carrying a 3-step SLA stepper / light one-row footer. The build is nav / hero (fill copy + a 420 hairline card with title, outcome and two chips) / bare-name industry tiles / a categories section / a manufacturers section / an ink credibility-and-CTA band / a dark multi-column footer. Two whole designed zones — the metric stats band and the SLA process stepper — were never built anywhere on this page, and the mock's signature device (an inline accent-filled box around the last word of each headline, used three times, and named as the chosen archetype in `.decision-log.md:17`) never entered DESIGN.md and so never entered the code. In exchange the build added two FR-mandated zones the mock lacks (categories FR8, OEM partners FR10) plus a full set of empty/fallback states, `lang`-marked fallback content, responsive ladders and a hamburger — real work the desktop-only mock never had to consider, and several places where the build correctly overrode the mock (mock section titles at 34px and section padding at 72 both exceed DESIGN.md's 24–28 / 44–64 ranges; the build's certs-beneath-the-hero placement is what FR10 actually requires). The single most consequential loss is not visual: the hero proof card in the mock is the doorway — it has the "I have a similar project" CTA that EXPERIENCE.md's Flow 1 names as its climax — and the shipped card is an unclickable dead end with no CTA and no link at all. Second is the industry card, which shipped as a name in a box while the resolved `description` sits unused and the sibling `/industries` index renders the exact anatomy the mock specified.

The divergences fall into three clean buckets. (1) One half of the footer was never built: the mock's `AddBtn` "Add to inquiry" outline button is absent, which also collapses the footer from a `space_between` two-slot bar into a single left-aligned link — and because the build renders the footer ONLY when a datasheet exists, some cards have no footer at all, a state the mock never contemplated. This is a documented DP-12 deferral to Epic 3, not an accident. (2) The build hardened the mock in ways that should stand: every small string moved from `$muted` (3.1:1 on `surface` — an AA failure at 11px) to `ink-2` (6.0:1); spec values moved from `$font-body` to `font-data`, which is what DESIGN.md's "if a machine produced it, it's data mono" rule requires and what the mock's OWN detail spec table does; body padding went from 16 (below DESIGN.md's 18–24 card-padding band) to 20; and the card became a stretched-overlay link to the detail page, an affordance the static mock could not express. (3) A handful of small losses the mock is right about and nobody has re-litigated: title leading 1.2 → browser default 1.5, per-product thumb icons → one universal `Package`, no-divider spec rows → per-row hairlines, and the `download` glyph. The recovery also resolves an old argument in the build's favour but for the wrong reason: the mock really does lay these cards out 4-up on the industry and accessories rows (3-up only in the catalog), so the "4 columns came from the missing mock" claim was accurate — EXPERIENCE.md's 3→2→1 ladder simply overrode it, and the two spines now openly contradict each other on a point a future implementer will trip over.

spine.overall_fidelity: The spines captured the canvas's *skeleton* with unusual precision and lost most of its *anatomy*. Everything that could be written as a rule survived: the 13 tokens are byte-identical; the 1440/100/1240 layout frame is exact; DESIGN.md:129's five fixed side-column widths (quote 420, facts 380, RFQ sidebar 360, applications panel 420, CTA column 320) are all five verifiable on the canvas to the pixel; the spec-row spec (DESIGN.md:163) matches outline:846-848 attribute for attribute; the breadcrumb spec (DESIGN.md:159) matches outline:773-780 exactly; the admin shell (DESIGN.md:170) matches outline:397-434 including the #1E2A3A active fill and the accent-soft left bar; the primary nav list matches all six nav copies and the shipped NAV_ITEMS three ways. The screen inventory is also correct — DESIGN.md:65's "7 screens + the Product Card component" is exactly what the canvas holds, EXPERIENCE.md's seven ● surfaces each have a frame, and every ○ surface (Services, About, Certificates/Downloads, admin CMS, all responsive variants) genuinely has none. **There is no mis-marking**: the ○ symbols are accurate, and the decision log's own "Mock coverage" line (.decision-log.md:122) says the same thing. The episode's root cause is not a wrong ○ — it is that DESIGN.md:65 named a machine-local, tool-internal `.pen` path as "source of truth for layout" and the optional export step was skipped. What did not survive is everything expressed as *drawing* rather than *rule*: a signature boxed-accent headline device used three times exists in neither spine nor code; roughly eight recurring components (stat block, process stepper, gallery, document row, project card, category tile, search bar, facet row) are drawn on the canvas and absent from DESIGN.md § Components, so each was re-invented at build time; and where the spine does name a number it is frequently narrower than the canvas it was distilled from (section padding, card padding, button sizes, type scale). In two places the spine and its own canvas flatly contradict each other — RFQ form labels and the kicker colour on light surfaces — and in both the spine is the one that needs to change.

briefs.summary:
NOTHING TO RECONCILE — `src/components/rfq/` is an empty directory and there is no `src/app/[locale]/(public)/rfq/` route. This is a pure brief.

WHAT THE MOCK SPECIFIES. The RFQ is a full standalone page, not a modal and not a section of Contact. Its outer frame is `fill=$surface-2` — the page ground is the grey step, and every card sits on it in white. That is an inversion of every other GLH page (which is `surface` with `surface-2` insets) and it is the single most load-bearing layout fact here: it is what makes two bordered white form cards read as a *document to fill in* rather than as page furniture. There is exactly ONE content section, `padding=[44,100] gap=44`, laid out horizontally: a `fill_container` form column (836px at the 1440 canvas) beside a fixed 360px side rail. That is the canonical two-column pattern and `TwoColumn`'s default `sideWidth` is already 360 (`src/components/ui/TwoColumn.tsx:53`) — it fits without a parameter, but its gap is hard-coded `gap-5` (20px) against the mock's 44, so it needs a gap prop or a `className` override.

The form column is five stacked blocks at `gap=24`: a heading pair, the clearable pre-fill banner, two numbered section cards, and a submit block. The two section cards ("1 · Your project", "2 · Your details") share one chrome: `surface` fill, 1px `border-subtle`, a header strip with a bottom hairline at `padding=[16,20]` carrying a Geist 16/600 title, and a body at `padding=20 gap=18`. That header/body split is a real reusable component the mock uses twice and no shipped component provides.

Every field is the same anatomy: an uppercase mono 11 label tracked at 1, a 7px gap, then a control at `padding=[11,14]` with a 1px border, 14px text, `$ink` when filled and `$muted` when placeholder. Selects add a right-aligned 16px `chevron-down` in `$ink-2` via `space_between`. Half-width pairs sit in horizontal rows at `gap=16`. Three controls break the pattern and are the genuinely new work: the EQUIPMENT chips-input (a bordered box that *contains* removable chips plus a trailing "+ Add equipment" accent link — the chips live inside the control, not beside it), the 96px-fixed-height textarea, and the dropzone (`surface-2` fill, `$muted` 1px stroke, centered `cloud-upload` 20px + a single line that states format and cap in one breath).

The side rail is three cards at `gap=20` and it is doing the whole "no prices" argument. Top: a dark `$ink` SLA card whose three steps each pair a 46×34 outlined badge holding a *data-mono* figure ("24h", "3 days", "→") with a title+description block. The third badge is a literal arrow, not a number — the third step deliberately has no promised duration, which is the honest thing and must not be "fixed" into "5 days". Middle: a white "Prefer to talk?" card with the phone set 20px in mono accent — the phone is typographically the *largest* element in the rail, which is how the mock delivers FR31's co-equality. Bottom: a `surface-2` borderless card that answers the objection head-on under a "WHY NO PRICES?" kicker, closing with four bare cert marks (`ISO 9001 · CE · EN · A.TR`) as plain mono 12 text — NOT `Chip` components, no boxes, no `badge-check`.

Sharp corners and flat throughout — the recovered JSON contains zero `cornerRadius`, `shadow`, `opacity` or `blur` keys anywhere in this frame. The frame has NO breadcrumb (unlike the product/project/industry mocks) and NO footer node; treat the missing breadcrumb as deliberate (a conversion endpoint is not a browse node) and the missing footer as the layout's job.

WHAT THE MOCK DOES NOT SPECIFY, AND THE STORY MUST. There is no confirmation/success state, no inline error state, no consent-blocked message, no attachment-rejected message and no rate-limit rejection — yet Story 3.2's AC, FR32, and UX-DR22 require all of them. The submitted-confirmation restating the SLA plus a reference is arguably the most important screen in Epic 3 and the canvas simply does not contain it. Design it from the SLA card (reuse it verbatim on the confirmation) rather than inventing a second visual language.

WHERE THE MOCK MUST LOSE. Three of its choices collide with floors this repo has already enforced and lost arguments over: (a) the field labels and the submit note are `$muted`, which the shipped `Kicker` component documents as 3.10:1 on white and 2.89:1 on `surface-2` against a 4.5 floor (`src/components/ui/Kicker.tsx:14-30`) — ship them `text-ink-2`; (b) the control borders are `$border-subtle` (#E6E9EE, ≈1.2:1 on white) which fails WCAG 1.4.11 for control boundaries, and `SearchForm` already set the precedent by using `border-muted` on exactly this kind of input (`src/components/catalog/SearchForm.tsx:56`); (c) `padding=[11,14]` around 14px text yields a ~41px control, under the 44px floor in UX-DR27 — add `min-h-11`. None of these change how the page reads; all three are non-negotiable.
structure: PAGE GROUND — outline:602. `frame "RFQ — Desktop" {width=1440 fill=$surface-2 layout=vertical}`. The whole page ground is surface-2 (#F5F7FA), NOT surface. Cards are white on grey. This is inverted from every other GLH page and is deliberate: it makes the two form cards read as a document. Only two children: Top Nav, RFQ Content. No breadcrumb node, no footer node, no cornerRadius/shadow keys anywhere in the frame.

TOP NAV — outline:603-623. The per-screen copy of the shared nav. UX-DR4 (epics:167) explicitly says these mock copies are replaced by the one component: reuse `src/components/layout/SiteHeader.tsx` unchanged. Facts for cross-checking only: surface fill, bottom hairline, padding [20,100]; brand mark 26px $brand box with white Geist 16/700 'G' + wordmark; nav links Inter 14 $ink-2 at gap 28; right cluster gap 16 = EN/TR/RU mono 12 switcher, phone in mono 13 $ink, navy CTA padding [10,18] with a white Inter 14/600 label. Note the nav CTA on THIS page still reads 'Request Project Quote' — the mock does not give it an active/current state.

RFQ CONTENT SECTION — outline:624. `{width=fill_container gap=44 padding=[44,100]}` — no `layout` prop, so HORIZONTAL. At the 1440 canvas: inner content 1240, side 360 fixed, gap 44, therefore the form column resolves to 836px. Use `TwoColumn` (src/components/ui/TwoColumn.tsx) whose default sideWidth is ALREADY 360 — but override its hard-coded `gap-5` (20px) to 44px; it exposes no gap prop today. The 100px gutter is `CONTAINER` (src/components/layout/container.ts).
FORM COLUMN — outline:625. `{width=fill_container layout=vertical gap=24}`. Five blocks: Head, Prefill Banner, Card 1, Card 2, Submit Block.

1. RFQ HEAD — outline:626-628. Vertical, gap 8. H1: Geist 34/700, letterSpacing -0.5, $ink, 'Request a project quote'. Sub: Inter 15, lineHeight 1.5, $ink-2, full-width fixed-growth. One h1 per page (UX-DR26).

2. PRE-FILL BANNER — outline:629-633. THE doorway artifact (UX-DR17, EXPERIENCE.md:97 calls it 'the single most important interaction on the site'). `fill=$surface` on the grey ground, `stroke=$accent strokeWidth={"left":3}` — a 3px navy rule on the LEFT EDGE ONLY, no other border. padding [12,16], gap 12, justify space_between, align center. Left group at gap 10: a 16px lucide `sparkles` in $accent + Inter 13 $ink text. Right: 'Clear' as $accent Inter 13/600 — text, not a button chrome, but it MUST be a real <button> with a ≥44px hit area and a visible focus ring. Banner renders only when pre-fill context is present; clearing it empties the pre-filled values, it does not just hide the banner.

3. CARD SHELL (used twice, new component) — outline:634-637 and 668-671. `{width=fill_container fill=$surface stroke=$border-subtle strokeWidth=1 layout=vertical}` → head `{stroke=$border-subtle strokeWidth={"bottom":1} padding=[16,20]}` carrying a Geist 16/600 $ink title → body `{layout=vertical gap=18 padding=20}`. The numeral is part of the title string ('1 · Your project'), not a separate badge.

4. FIELD ANATOMY (13 instances) — e.g. outline:639-643. Group: `{layout=vertical gap=7}`. Label: `$font-mono` 11, `$muted`, letterSpacing 1, UPPERCASE. Control box: `{fill=$surface stroke=$border-subtle strokeWidth=1 padding=[11,14] justifyContent=space_between alignItems=center}`; value text Inter 14, `$ink` filled / `$muted` placeholder, `textGrowth=fixed-width`. SELECTS append a 16px `chevron-down` in `$ink-2`. Half-width pairs sit in a horizontal row frame at `gap=16` with both children `fill_container`. SHIP-TIME CORRECTIONS: label → `text-ink-2` (muted fails AA at 11px); border → `border-muted` (border-subtle fails 1.4.11); add `min-h-11` (the mock's box computes to ~41px).

4a. CARD 1 · YOUR PROJECT, body rows — outline:637-667. Row 1 (gap 16): INDUSTRY select (shows 'Logistics') | TIMELINE select (placeholder 'Select timeline…'). Then full-width: EQUIPMENT chips-input. Then full-width: PROJECT DESCRIPTION textarea. Then full-width: SPEC / DRAWING (OPTIONAL) dropzone.

4b. EQUIPMENT CHIPS-INPUT — outline:649-658. The label is 'EQUIPMENT'. The control is a box `{stroke=$border-subtle strokeWidth=1 gap=8 padding=[10,12] alignItems=center}` that CONTAINS the chips — chips are inside the input, not below it. Each chip: `{fill=$surface-2 stroke=$border-subtle strokeWidth=1 gap=6 padding=[5,10]}` with an Inter 13 $ink label and a 13px lucide `x` in `$muted`. A trailing 'Add equipment' affordance rendered as accent Inter 13 with a literal '+ ' prefix in the string. The x must be a real button with an accessible name ('Remove Fire suppression') and a ≥44px hit area on mobile; the 13px muted x is a 3.10:1 non-text glyph and should darken to ink-2.

4c. PROJECT DESCRIPTION — outline:659-662. Label 'PROJECT DESCRIPTION'. Box `{height=96 layout=vertical padding=[12,14]}` — a FIXED 96px height, not auto-grow. Placeholder Inter 14 $muted lineHeight 1.5.

4d. DROPZONE — outline:663-667. Label 'SPEC / DRAWING (OPTIONAL)' — the optionality is in the LABEL, not a separate hint. Box `{fill=$surface-2 stroke=$muted strokeWidth=1 gap=10 padding=[18,16] justifyContent=center alignItems=center}` — horizontal, centered, SOLID 1px muted stroke (the recovered JSON has no dash key anywhere; DESIGN.md:169's 'dashed hairline' is not what the canvas holds). 20px lucide `cloud-upload` in $ink-2 + a single Inter 13 $ink-2 line stating action and constraints together. FR32a's 15 MB cap and the PDF/XLSX/DWG allowlist are stated up front, in the control, before the user picks a file.

4e. CARD 2 · YOUR DETAILS — outline:668-700. Three horizontal rows at gap 16, card body gap 18. Row d1: FULL NAME | COMPANY (text, placeholder-filled). Row d2: WORK EMAIL | PHONE (text). Row d3: COUNTRY | PREFERRED LANGUAGE (both selects, both shown FILLED — 'Turkey' and 'English' in $ink — i.e. they are pre-defaulted from locale/geo, not empty). Note the label is 'WORK EMAIL', not 'EMAIL' — a deliberate B2B qualifier.

5. SUBMIT BLOCK — outline:701-709. Vertical, gap 16. (a) Consent row `{gap=10}`: an 18×18 box `{fill=$surface stroke=$ink strokeWidth=1.5}` — sharp, 1.5px ink, matching the secondary-button stroke weight — beside `fill_container` Inter 13 $ink-2 lineHeight 1.5 consent copy. The 18px box needs a ≥44px label hit area. open_questions: Is `/rfq` a distinct page from `/contact`, or is the Contact page (FR33, Story 3.8) this same form plus a map and legal details? The mock is a standalone page with a side rail whose middle card is already a contact block, so the two surfaces overlap by ~60%. Does the RFQ page render the site footer? The recovered frame has only Top Nav + RFQ Content — no footer node. Every other frame likely behaves the same (the nav is also copied per-screen), so this is probably a canvas convention rather than a decision, but a conversion page with no footer is a defensible choice worth making deliberately.

What is the full pre-fill param contract for Story 3.4? `?q=` is already shipped and binding (SearchEmptyState.tsx:23-25). What are the names for product, category, industry and project — and does the banner text come from resolving those IDs server-side (translatable, fallback-markable) or from a literal label in the URL (unvalidated, spoofable, and an XSS surface if echoed)? Prefer IDs resolved server-side.

Is '+ Add equipment' a typeahead over PID products, over categories, or free text? FR27 says 'equipment categories/products' — both. The chips-input must distinguish a resolved PID reference from a typed string, because `Lead.equipment` is `Json` and an admin reading the lead needs to know which is which.

Where do quantities live — a per-chip numeric stepper inside the EQUIPMENT control, a separate field, or folded into the description? FR27 requires them and `Lead.quantities` is a single `String?`, which hints at free text; the mock offers no affordance at all.
What are the TIMELINE options, and is the field required? No source document specifies them.
Is COUNTRY a fixed ISO list or free text? `Lead.country` is `String?`. The mock shows it pre-filled with 'Turkey', implying geo/locale defaulting — from what signal?

Does the confirmation render on the same route (a state swap, preserving the form for analytics) or at `/rfq/thanks`? This determines whether the 'reference' is addressable, whether a refresh resubmits, and how a conversion event is fired.

What form does the 'reference' take? Story 3.2's AC requires one; `Lead.id` is a cuid, which is unreadable over the phone. A short human-quotable ref (e.g. GLH-2026-0042) needs a column or a derivation rule.

Is the SLA card the same component on the RFQ, the confirmation, and the Contact page — and does Story 3.5's content model back all three? Building it three times is how the '24h / 3 days' numbers drift apart, which UX-DR28 explicitly forbids.

Does the side rail stick on scroll? The form column is tall (two cards plus a submit block) and the rail is short; nothing in the canvas expresses stickiness, but an 836px form scrolling past a dead rail wastes the conversion anchor.

How does this collapse below `lg`? EXPERIENCE.md:157 and UX-DR27 require a sticky bottom CTA bar (Request quote / Call) on mobile — but on the RFQ page the 'Request quote' action IS the page, so the bar presumably reduces to Call. And where do the three rail cards land when stacked: all above the form (delaying the form), all below (unread), or the SLA card above and the rest below?

Is the `sparkles` icon on the pre-fill banner right for this register? It is a valid lucide line icon and DESIGN.md permits the family, but it reads consumer-AI against an engineer-to-engineer voice. `wand-2`, `link` or `corner-down-right` would say 'carried from where you came' more literally.

Does the honeypot field (FR32) need a visual slot at all, and how is it hidden without breaking the screen-reader pass? Off-screen positioning plus `aria-hidden` and `tabindex=-1` is the usual answer, but it must be written down because `display:none` defeats most bots' filters.

briefs.summary:
The mock specifies a nine-zone case-study page, and it is materially richer than what Story 3.1's acceptance criteria describe. Top nav → breadcrumb → a full-bleed 360px-high "Image Band" → a two-column Overview (narrative left, a 380px Project Facts anchor card right) → a four-cell stat band on `ink` → a "Scope of supply" BOM table → a four-card equipment row of real `ProductCard`s → a five-step "How we delivered" process strip → a three-card "More in oil & gas" related row → a closing CTA band on `ink`. The page reads as proof-then-doorway: every zone is evidence, and two CTA clusters (the sticky-feeling facts card, and the closing band) both route to the pre-filled RFQ.

Four things in it are genuinely load-bearing and worth taking whole. (1) The **Image Band is the no-photo state, drawn deliberately** — not a missing asset. briefs.summary:
The mock specifies a two-region admin: a fixed 244px `ink` sidebar and a light main region of three stacked strips — Topbar, Status Tabs, Leads Table. It is a list-only surface: seven lead rows, one link affordance per row, and nothing else. Every interaction the story requires beyond "see the list" is absent from the canvas — there is no lead-detail frame anywhere in the 8-frame canvas, no delete affordance, no pagination despite a "128 total" counter over 7 visible rows, no empty state, no sort controls, no bulk selection, and no sign-out control. Treat the mock as authoritative for the shell geometry, the column set, the tab model and the copy register; treat the missing pieces as work the story must design, not omit.

What the mock gets right and should be copied verbatim: the four-status model maps exactly onto the shipped `LeadStatus` enum (`prisma/schema.prisma:36-41` — new / in_review / quoted / closed), the tab counts are internally consistent (4+9+22+93 = 128), the status palette matches tokens that ALREADY EXIST in `src/app/globals.css:25-29` (`--color-status-new/review/quoted/closed`), and the REF cell is `$accent`-coloured — i.e. the row's link target is the reference cell, not a whole-row div-onclick. Build it as a real semantic `<table>` with `<th>` header cells (EXPERIENCE.md:114) and an `<a>` in the REF cell.

Three things in the mock must NOT be copied. (1) The status pills are drawn as solid fills with white 11px mono text; white on `status-new` #159A5B is 3.62:1, on `status-review` #C2870B is 3.10:1, on `status-closed` #8A93A0 is 3.10:1 — three of four fail AA for small text. DESIGN.md:166 already specifies the correct treatment ("rectangular tag ... text + small dot / tinted"), so use a tinted background with dark coloured text. (2) Every mono column header, the tab counts, and the topbar subtitle are `$muted` at 11–12px; `src/components/ui/Kicker.tsx:14-27` has already computed and documented that `muted` #8A93A0 is 3.10:1 on white and FAILS, and EXPERIENCE.md:109 directs such labels to darken toward `ink-2`. Every shipped surface honours this; the admin must too — `Kicker tone="ink"` is the ready-made answer. (3) The solid green count badge on the sidebar's Inquiries item is a second non-logo use of `brand` green, which DESIGN.md:103 forbids ("Its only non-logo use is the small new/success status dot and the cert badge-check glyph") — either re-tint the badge or amend DESIGN.md deliberately.

The one hard blocker: the mock's leading column is a human-readable reference, `GLH-RFQ-2041`. No such field exists. `prisma/schema.prisma:288-310` gives `Lead` a cuid `id` and nothing else identity-like, and no PRD FR, epic or architecture line mentions a reference number. Displaying a raw cuid in that column would destroy the mock's whole reading (a scannable, quotable, sequential reference an engineer can cite on the phone). This needs a schema addition plus a sequence, and it must be decided before the RFQ confirmation copy is written, because the customer-facing confirmation should quote the same reference.

Two data realities the mock papers over. `Lead.equipment` is `Json @default("[]")` (schema:291) — an array; the RFQ mock (outline:659-666) shows a user selecting two items ("Fire suppression", "Detection panels"), yet the EQUIPMENT column renders a single string. The column needs a summarise-and-overflow rule ("Fire suppression +1"). And `Lead.industry` is `String?` (schema:290), free text/slug rather than a relation to `Industry` — the column must resolve slug→label and handle null, or it will render "oil-gas" next to "Nuclear".

Does the chevron open a full detail page (/admin/leads/[id]) or a side drawer? A page is cheaper, links cleanly from the REF cell, and survives a browser refresh; a drawer keeps the list context. Nothing in the mock, the epics or the architecture decides it.
